title: US Senate Passes Two-Year Extension of Haiti HOPE/HELP Trade Programs
detail: The US Senate approved on August 11, 2026 a two-year extension of the Haiti HOPE and HELP trade preference programs — which grant duty-free US market access to Haitian apparel and textile exports — as part of a bipartisan interim funding resolution alongside the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA). The House previously passed its own version 340–54; the Senate's amended text must clear another House vote when Congress reconvenes in September 2026 before going to President Trump for signature. Sen. Raphael Warnock (D-GA), who helped secure the extension, called it 'a win-win for Georgians and our trading partners in Haiti and Africa.' The programs — Haiti's principal formal economic lifeline, underpinning tens of thousands of garment-sector jobs — had lapsed on September 30, 2025 and were only retroactively restored for 15 months in February 2026, underscoring the fragility of Haiti's export sector amid the ongoing security and economic crisis. CODEVI Group president Capellán Peralta said industry is still pushing for a full ten-year extension to attract new investment.
